stem:
The diagram shows Vihaan lighting an incense stick. It burns with a steady tip of glowing ash and smoke. He then covers the incense stick with a glass tumbler. After some time the glowing tip goes out.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: While it burns, the incense stick needs fuel, oxygen from the air, and heat above its ignition temperature.
Under the tumbler the glowing tip goes out when the oxygen inside runs low.
The incense stick catches fire as soon as it softens in air.
An incense stick left in air at room temperature will start burning without being heated.

teacher.key_rationale: Combustion needs fuel, oxygen, and enough heat to reach ignition temperature. Covering the stick limits oxygen so the glow goes out. Softening resin or room-temperature paper without heating does not start combustion.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source force diagram into covered incense stick.
